title: Haven’t even tried it yet
body:
Just giving 5 stars for the other unfair reviews. I know how damaging they can be :(

Thanks for offering a free option for low income people, that other guy was out of line I think.

I sympathise with his frustration though. It’s so rare to see ADHD “friendly” apps that do provide accessible payment options and don’t take advantage of people with ADHD. We are really susceptible to deceptive and manipulative IAPs. Endel appalled me in this regard… same for Headspace and many others.

Thanks again and all the best with your app and future endeavours 🙏 😊
author: RedRobin001

title: My Homeschooling Assistant
body: The biggest challenge in Homeschooling my time blind daughter was keeping her on task. She has responded so well to having the Weel wheel on the big screen of my laptop. She doesn’t need to ask me what the time is or what task she should be on as it’s a live view and shows her exactly where she’s at. She’s 9 years old and her primary distraction being her brother is 1. My husband works away 3 months at a time so my stress levels were peaking. Now we share the time pressure together, she’s always on time if not finishing earlier so she gets her ‘break’ between tasks. She loves the colours as well we have key learning in red and play in blue etc.
author: Family Homeschooling

title: It’s my go to
body: I have trialled a range of diary/organiser apps - trying to find something that keeps me focused without feeling like I have homework. This one hits the spot. As a neurodivergent clinical psychologist - this app makes me feel like I’m control of my day, my executive functioning is not chasing its tail. Thank you very much.
author: jodoyogo

title: Gave me a fun excuse to finally organise my calendar
body: Love the app. Love the widgets. Has helped immensely with time blindness and communication between my partner and I.
author: Annieeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

title: Love the visual
body: I like that i have a visual wheel to see my appointments at a glance
author: Furtivegal

title: $60 AUD to have more then two calendars is highway robbery
body:
Having a subscription model for a fairly uncomplicated visual planner feels like a highway robbery for me. A one time payment would be more acceptable.

Other then the price tag this app is great and anyone who is able to afford the steep price tag should get it… but if you can’t well there is like one other alternative that is cheaper and doesn’t require a monthly or yearly subscription.
author: Redatopia

title: Has potential, but needs more features no greater customisation
body:
I have ADHD so I fit the primary target demographic. 

PiCal appears to be only a new front end to apple calendars. It presents information graphically in variable time blocks and adds limited check list functionality.

I like the application as it has potential, but in my opinion is not worth even a fraction of the asking price. 

For me to buy this application it would need at least the following additional features:
(1) Ability to nominate start day of the week (Sunday, not Monday)
(2) Ability to edit checklists (without having to delete entire event)
(3) multiple checklists — one for task breakdowns and at least one more for what equipment, chemicals etc., that I should take for work at that location on that particular day
(4) I want to be able to populate my schedule for say every Monday but would want to be able to easily modify checklists for 1st, 2nd, 3rd. 4th and 5th week of the month etc. 
(5) Additional fields similar to location field. I want to be able to record phone numbers and other contact information for people I should contact at that location. Perhaps this could be a simple link to contacts …
author: DP down under

title: Great app
body:
Thanks, this app is a great concept and very good execution. 
While I’d love a few more features, what I  love more is that the features you’ve developed seem to work well. 
I wanted an app that shows how long until my next appointment and provides visual representation of that. This app is close!
